title: Interpreter use and patient-reported understanding: an umbrella review
abstract: Objective: to summarise what published reviews show about professional, bilingual-staff and ad hoc interpretation, and about video versus in-person interpretation, for patient-reported understanding. Design: umbrella review with AMSTAR 2 quality ratings and overlap assessment, reported against PRIOR. Results and conclusions will be written after the synthesis.
introduction: Many reviews address medical interpreting, but they overlap heavily and differ in quality, and patient-reported understanding is rarely measured. A widely repeated claim that video interpreting is equivalent to in-person interpreting could not be traced to any retrieved review.
methods: Registered protocol; library search of databases and review registries; dual screening; extraction per review; AMSTAR 2 ratings; citation matrix and corrected covered area; pre-specified rule for overlapping reviews; descriptive synthesis without re-pooling.
results: Not yet written. The section will present the flow of reviews, quality ratings, the overlap matrix and summary tables by comparison and outcome.
discussion: The discussion will separate supported conclusions from open questions, especially for video against in-person interpretation, and state implications for an interpreter standard.
limitations: Dependence on review quality and extraction; overlap; sparse evidence on understanding by mode.
conclusion: To be written after synthesis; it will not state that video and in-person interpreting are equivalent unless higher-confidence evidence is found.
summary: PRIOR-structured draft with results left empty until synthesis.
